frequency_question: How often does a major emerging market central bank deploy an incremental or secondary reserve ratio tool during periods of unexpected systemic liquidity surges?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement by a major emerging market central bank of a temporary secondary reserve ratio (such as incremental CRR) to absorb surplus liquidity. Excludes standard, permanent adjustments to baseline reserve requirement ratios.

cases.name: PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio Special/Targeted Adjustments
Bank of Korea Targeted Liquidity Adjustment Measures

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; represents targeted secondary reserve ratio deployments in major emerging markets.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or opaque administrative liquidity directives that did not take the formal structure of a reserve ratio.
skeleton: Central bank monetary policy tightening cycles involving surplus liquidity management across major emerging markets since 2000, broken down by distinct liquidity-surge regimes.
multiplier: 3 observed distinct deployments across comparable emerging market tightening phases over 25 years yielding an approximate baseline frequency of once every 8 to 10 years under specific surplus conditions.
validity_reason: Central bank operational toolkits and structural liquidity management frameworks evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
